newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian shares drop as volume down.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian shares drop as volume down.

text.p: Palestinian shares closed slightly down on Sunday with falling activity on the Palestinian Securities Exchange (PSE).

The Jerusalem Index closed at 101.07, down from 101.13 on Wednesday. Around 134,978 shares worth 237,542 Jordanian dinars changed hands, down from 168,545 shares worth 263,583 dinars traded on Wednesday.
Safwan Bataineh, PSE general manager said Sunday's trading session was quiet but for the drop in share prices of two companies, pushing the index downwards.
"It was a quiet day for us, and although we have two trading sessions a week now, the capital market is still in an infancy stage," Bataineh told Reuters.
Bataineh said the impasse in the peace process was scaring investors away.
PLO-Israeli peace moves have been suspended since Israel broke ground on a new Jewish settlement in occupied East Jerusalem last March.

Closures Israel imposed on Palestinian areas following suicide bombings which killed scores of people in the Jewish state last year have led to the deterioration of the already ailing Palestinian economy.
"However, the trading volume has improved. In June the volume traded was worth $50,000 per week, but it rose in July to $800,000 per week," he said.
"The listing of large companies coming next week should take trading levels still higher," Bataineh said.
In trading this week, the Arab Insurance Establishment fell one about percent to 2.95 dinars per share, and the National Insurance Co. dropped one percent to 1.95 dinars a share.
The Palestine Telecommunications Co, which accounted for over 80 percent of the total turnover, closed even at 1.47 dinars per share.
Trading is conducted in dollars or Jordanian dinars in the absence of a Palestinian currency.
